learning-groups.title: Find your constellation
learning-groups.teaser: Six moons. Three pairs. Can a little local knowledge help everyone learn?
learning-groups.prompt: Pair moons with similar temperatures. Find all three pairs and watch the prediction error shrink.
learning-groups.note: A toy analogy for client grouping, not a privacy guarantee or a reproduction of the method.
learning-groups.connection: Different clients have different data. Grouping related clients can help personalize what they learn together.

rover-coordination.title: Lost Rovers
rover-coordination.teaser: Three rovers, an unknown planet, and twelve rounds to find your way.
rover-coordination.prompt: Recover three supply pods in 12 rounds. Select a rover, tap a neighboring tile to plan its step, then move the team.
rover-coordination.note: An exploration toy. The paper studies probabilistic evidence fusion and coordinated planning under explicit assumptions.
rover-coordination.connection: Shared observations reveal more of the map. Seeing teammates’ plans helps avoid repeated exploration. Try both map modes on the same planet.

risk-check.title: Mission control
risk-check.teaser: The next launch is your call. Is there enough evidence to go?
risk-check.prompt: Review three missions. Launch when the entire risk range is at or below 20%; otherwise take a reading or hold.
risk-check.note: Illustrative risk ranges in a fictional model. These are not real safety estimates.
risk-check.connection: A safety claim depends on both a model and the evidence. New observations can change what a system has reason to do.
